passages.text: Then Rehoboam went to Shechem, for all Israel had gone there to make him king.
passages.sermon:
Rehoboam was the son of Solomon.
Rehoboam became king after Solomon died.
Rehoboam went to Shechem.
All Israel had gone to Shechem.
The people of Israel went there to make Rehoboam king.
passages.original: וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ רְחַבְעָ֖ם שְׁכֶ֑מָה כִּ֥י שְׁכֶ֛ם בָּ֥אוּ כָל־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לְהַמְלִ֥יךְ אֹתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: When Jeroboam son of Nebat heard about this, he returned from Egypt, where he had fled from King Solomon.
passages.sermon:
Jeroboam was the son of Nebat.
Jeroboam was in Egypt.
Jeroboam had fled to Egypt.
Jeroboam fled from King Solomon.
Jeroboam heard about Solomon’s death and Rehoboam becoming king.
Jeroboam returned from Egypt.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֞י כִּשְׁמֹ֨עַ יָרָבְעָ֤ם בֶּן־ נְבָט֙ וְה֣וּא בְמִצְרַ֔יִם אֲשֶׁ֣ר בָּרַ֔ח מִפְּנֵ֖י שְׁלֹמֹ֣ה הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַיָּ֥שָׁב יָרָבְעָ֖ם מִמִּצְרָֽיִם׃

passages.text: So they sent for Jeroboam, and he and all Israel came to Rehoboam and said, “Your father put a heavy yoke on us. But now you should lighten the burden of your father’s service and the heavy yoke he put on us, and we will serve you.”
passages.sermon:
Jeroboam was in Egypt.
The people of Israel sent for Jeroboam.
Jeroboam came to Rehoboam.
All Israel came with Jeroboam.
They spoke to Rehoboam.
They said, “Your father made our burden heavy.
He gave us hard service.
He put a heavy yoke on us.
Now make our work lighter.
Take away the heavy yoke your father put on us.
If you do this, we will serve you.”
passages.original: וַֽיִּשְׁלְחוּ֙ וַיִּקְרְאוּ־ ל֔וֹ וַיָּבֹ֥א יָרָבְעָ֖ם וְכָל־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַֽיְדַבְּר֔וּ אֶל־ רְחַבְעָ֖ם לֵאמֹֽר׃ אָבִ֖יךָ הִקְשָׁ֣ה אֶת־ עֻלֵּ֑נוּ וְעַתָּ֡ה הָקֵל֩ מֵעֲבֹדַ֨ת אָבִ֜יךָ הַקָּשָׁ֗ה וּמֵעֻלּ֧וֹ הַכָּבֵ֛ד אֲשֶׁר־ נָתַ֥ן עָלֵ֖ינוּ וְנַֽעַבְדֶֽךָּ׃

passages.text: Rehoboam answered, “Come back to me in three days.” So the people departed.
passages.sermon:
Rehoboam was the king.
Rehoboam spoke to the people.
He said, “Return to me after three days.”
The people left.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲלֵהֶ֗ם ע֛וֹד שְׁלֹ֥שֶׁת יָמִ֖ים וְשׁ֣וּבוּ אֵלָ֑י וַיֵּ֖לֶךְ הָעָֽם׃ס

passages.text: Then King Rehoboam consulted with the elders who had served his father Solomon during his lifetime. “How do you advise me to respond to these people?” he asked.
passages.sermon:
King Rehoboam was the son of Solomon.
Solomon was king before Rehoboam.
Rehoboam became king after Solomon died.
Rehoboam wanted advice.
He went to the elders.
These elders had served Solomon.
They had served Solomon while he was alive.
Rehoboam spoke to the elders.
He asked them a question.
He said, “How do you advise me?”
He wanted to know how to answer the people.
He asked, “How should I respond to these people?”
passages.original: וַיִּוָּעַ֞ץ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ רְחַבְעָ֗ם אֶת־ הַזְּקֵנִים֙ אֲשֶׁר־ הָי֣וּ עֹֽמְדִ֗ים לִפְנֵי֙ שְׁלֹמֹ֣ה אָבִ֔יו בִּֽהְיֹת֥וֹ חַ֖י לֵאמֹ֑ר אֵ֚יךְ אַתֶּ֣ם נֽוֹעָצִ֔ים לְהָשִׁ֥יב לָֽעָם־ הַזֶּ֖ה דָּבָֽר׃

passages.text: They replied, “If you will be kind to these people and please them by speaking kind words to them, they will be your servants forever.”
passages.sermon:
The elders spoke to King Rehoboam.
They said, "Be good to these people."
Show kindness to them.
Speak kind words to them.
If you do this, they will serve you always.
They will be your servants for all your days.
passages.original: וַיְדַבְּר֨וּ אֵלָ֜יו לֵאמֹ֗ר אִם־ תִּֽהְיֶ֨ה לְט֜וֹב לְהָעָ֤ם הַזֶּה֙ וּרְצִיתָ֔ם וְדִבַּרְתָּ֥ אֲלֵהֶ֖ם דְּבָרִ֣ים טוֹבִ֑ים וְהָי֥וּ לְךָ֛ עֲבָדִ֖ים כָּל־ הַיָּמִֽים׃

passages.text: But Rehoboam rejected the advice of the elders; instead, he consulted the young men who had grown up with him and served him.
passages.sermon:
Rehoboam was the king of Israel.
He received advice from the elders who had served his father Solomon.
Rehoboam rejected the advice of these elders.
He chose not to follow their counsel.
Rehoboam then consulted the young men.
These young men had grown up with him.
They stood before him and served him.
Rehoboam asked these young men for advice.
passages.original: וַֽיַּעֲזֹ֛ב אֶת־ עֲצַ֥ת הַזְּקֵנִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר יְעָצֻ֑הוּ וַיִּוָּעַ֗ץ אֶת־ הַיְלָדִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר גָּדְל֣וּ אִתּ֔וֹ הָעֹמְדִ֖ים לְפָנָֽיו׃

passages.text: He asked them, “What message do you advise that we send back to these people who have spoken to me, saying, ‘Lighten the yoke your father put on us’?”
passages.sermon:
Rehoboam was the new king of Israel.
He spoke to the young men who grew up with him.
He asked them a question.
He said, “What advice do you give me?”
He wanted to know what message to send to the people.
The people had come to him with a request.
They said, “Your father put a heavy yoke on us.”
They asked Rehoboam to make their burden lighter.
Rehoboam asked the young men, “How should we answer these people?”
He wanted to know what to say to those who asked for a lighter yoke.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲלֵהֶ֗ם מָ֚ה אַתֶּ֣ם נֽוֹעָצִ֔ים וְנָשִׁ֥יב דָּבָ֖ר אֶת־ הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֑ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר דִּבְּר֤וּ אֵלַי֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר הָקֵל֙ מִן־ הָעֹ֔ל אֲשֶׁר־ נָתַ֥ן אָבִ֖יךָ עָלֵֽינוּ׃

passages.text: The young men who had grown up with him replied, “This is how you should answer these people who said to you, ‘Your father made our yoke heavy, but you should make it lighter.’ This is what you should tell them: ‘My little finger is thicker than my father’s waist!
passages.sermon:
Rehoboam was the king of Israel.
Young men grew up with Rehoboam.
These young men served Rehoboam.
The young men spoke to Rehoboam.
They gave him advice.
They said, "Speak to the people this way."
The people said to Rehoboam, "Your father made our yoke heavy."
The people asked Rehoboam, "Make our burden lighter."
The young men told Rehoboam, "Say this to the people."
"My little finger is thicker than my father's waist."
passages.original: וַיְדַבְּר֣וּ אִתּ֗וֹ הַיְלָדִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֨ר גָּדְל֣וּ אִתּוֹ֮ לֵאמֹר֒ כֹּֽה־ תֹאמַ֡ר לָעָם֩ אֲשֶׁר־ דִּבְּר֨וּ אֵלֶ֜יךָ לֵאמֹ֗ר אָבִ֙יךָ֙ הִכְבִּ֣יד אֶת־ עֻלֵּ֔נוּ וְאַתָּ֖ה הָקֵ֣ל מֵעָלֵ֑ינוּ כֹּ֚ה תֹּאמַ֣ר אֲלֵהֶ֔ם קָֽטָנִּ֥י עָבָ֖ה מִמָּתְנֵ֥י אָבִֽי׃

passages.text: Whereas my father burdened you with a heavy yoke, I will add to your yoke. Whereas my father scourged you with whips, I will scourge you with scorpions.’ ”
passages.sermon:
King Rehoboam spoke to the people of Israel.
He said his father, King Solomon, gave them a heavy burden.
He said, "My father put a heavy yoke on you."
He said, "I will make your yoke even heavier."
He said, "My father punished you with whips."
He said, "I will punish you with scorpions."
passages.original: וְעַתָּ֗ה אָבִי֙ הֶעְמִ֤יס עֲלֵיכֶם֙ עֹ֣ל כָּבֵ֔ד וַאֲנִ֖י אֹסִ֣יף עַֽל־ עֻלְּכֶ֑ם אָבִ֗י יִסַּ֤ר אֶתְכֶם֙ בַּשּׁוֹטִ֔ים וַאֲנִ֖י בָּֽעֲקְרַבִּֽים׃ס

passages.text: After three days, Jeroboam and all the people returned to Rehoboam, since the king had said, “Come back to me on the third day.”
passages.sermon:
King Rehoboam ruled over Israel after Solomon.
Jeroboam was a leader among the people of Israel.
Three days passed.
Jeroboam and all the people came to Rehoboam.
They came on the third day.
Rehoboam had told them, “Come back to me on the third day.”
The people obeyed the king’s command.
They returned to Rehoboam as he had said.
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֨א יָרָבְעָ֧ם וְכָל־ הָעָ֛ם אֶל־ רְחַבְעָ֖ם בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁלִשִׁ֑י כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר דִּבֶּ֤ר הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר שׁ֥וּבוּ אֵלַ֖י בַּיּ֥וֹם הַשְּׁלִשִֽׁי׃

passages.text: And the king answered them harshly. King Rehoboam rejected the advice of the elders and spoke to them as the young men had advised, saying, “Whereas my father made your yoke heavy, I will add to your yoke. Whereas my father scourged you with whips, I will scourge you with scorpions.”
passages.sermon:
King Rehoboam was the ruler of Israel at this time.
He spoke to the people.
He answered them harshly.
He did not follow the advice of the elders.
He rejected the elders’ advice.
He followed the advice of the young men instead.
He said to the people, “My father made your yoke heavy.
I will make your yoke even heavier.
My father punished you with whips.
I will punish you with scorpions.”
passages.original: וַיַּעֲנֵ֥ם הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ קָשָׁ֑ה וַֽיַּעֲזֹב֙ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ רְחַבְעָ֔ם אֵ֖ת עֲצַ֥ת הַזְּקֵנִֽים׃ וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר אֲלֵהֶ֗ם כַּעֲצַ֤ת הַיְלָדִים֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר אַכְבִּיד֙ אֶֽת־ עֻלְּכֶ֔ם וַאֲנִ֖י אֹסִ֣יף עָלָ֑יו אָבִ֗י יִסַּ֤ר אֶתְכֶם֙ בַּשּׁוֹטִ֔ים וַאֲנִ֖י בָּעֲקְרַבִּֽים׃

passages.text: So the king did not listen to the people, and indeed this turn of events was from God, in order that the LORD might fulfill the word that He had spoken through Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam son of Nebat.
passages.sermon:
King Rehoboam did not listen to the people.
God caused this to happen.
God wanted to fulfill His word.
The LORD had spoken this word before.
God spoke through Ahijah the Shilonite.
God gave this message to Jeroboam son of Nebat.
passages.original: וְלֹֽא־ שָׁמַ֥ע הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ אֶל־ הָעָ֑ם כִּֽי־ הָיְתָ֤ה נְסִבָּה֙ מֵעִ֣ם הָֽאֱלֹהִ֔ים לְמַעַן֩ הָקִ֨ים יְהוָ֜ה אֶת־ דְּבָר֗וֹ אֲשֶׁ֤ר דִּבֶּר֙ בְּיַד֙ אֲחִיָּ֣הוּ הַשִּֽׁלוֹנִ֔י אֶל־ יָרָבְעָ֖ם בֶּן־ נְבָֽט׃

passages.text: When all Israel saw that the king had refused to listen to them, they answered the king: “What portion do we have in David, and what inheritance in the son of Jesse? To your tents, O Israel! Look now to your own house, O David!” So all the Israelites went home, but Rehoboam still reigned over the Israelites living in the cities of Judah.
passages.sermon:
King Rehoboam was the ruler of Israel after Solomon.
Rehoboam refused to listen to the people of Israel.
All Israel saw that the king did not listen to them.
The people answered the king.
They said, “We have no share in David.
We have no inheritance in the son of Jesse.
Israel, go to your tents.
David, look after your own house.”
All the Israelites went home.
Rehoboam continued to rule over the Israelites who lived in the cities of Judah.
passages.original: וְכָל־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל כִּ֠י לֹא־ שָׁמַ֣ע הַמֶּלֶךְ֮ לָהֶם֒ וַיָּשִׁ֣יבוּ הָעָ֣ם אֶת־ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ׀ לֵאמֹ֡ר מַה־ לָּנוּ֩ חֵ֨לֶק בְּדָוִ֜יד וְלֹֽא־ נַחֲלָ֣ה בְּבֶן־ יִשַׁ֗י אִ֤ישׁ לְאֹהָלֶ֙יךָ֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל עַתָּ֕ה רְאֵ֥ה בֵיתְךָ֖ דָּוִ֑יד וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ כָּל־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לְאֹהָלָֽיו׃ס וּבְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל הַיֹּֽשְׁבִ֖ים בְּעָרֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֑ה וַיִּמְלֹ֥ךְ עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם רְחַבְעָֽם׃

passages.text: Then King Rehoboam sent out Hadoram, who was in charge of the forced labor, but the Israelites stoned him to death. And King Rehoboam mounted his chariot in haste and escaped to Jerusalem.
passages.sermon:
King Rehoboam ruled over Judah.
Hadoram managed the forced labor for King Rehoboam.
King Rehoboam sent Hadoram to the Israelites.
The Israelites stoned Hadoram.
Hadoram died.
King Rehoboam quickly got into his chariot.
King Rehoboam fled to Jerusalem.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁלַ֞ח הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ רְחַבְעָ֗ם אֶת־ הֲדֹרָם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עַל־ הַמַּ֔ס וַיִּרְגְּמוּ־ ב֧וֹ בְנֵֽי־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל אֶ֖בֶן וַיָּמֹ֑ת וְהַמֶּ֣לֶךְ רְחַבְעָ֗ם הִתְאַמֵּץ֙ לַֽעֲל֣וֹת בַּמֶּרְכָּבָ֔ה לָנ֖וּס יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃ס

passages.text: So to this day Israel has been in rebellion against the house of David.
passages.sermon: Israel rebelled against the house of David.\r\nThis rebellion continued until today.
passages.original: וַיִּפְשְׁע֤וּ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ בְּבֵ֣ית דָּוִ֔יד עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃ס
